english.title: Obtain property from subject of a debt relief order knowing or believing money is owed
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), during the relevant period as defined in section 251R(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986,

(A)_[acquired]_
(B)_[received]_

property, namely **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..), from **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person in respect of whom a debt relief order had been made, knowing or believing that that person owed money in respect of the property and that

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

did not intend, or was unlikely to be able, to pay the money

(E)_[he]_
(F)_[she]_

so owed
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 251R(2), 251T(3) and 430 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
obtain property from subject of debt relief order
knowing / believing that debtor did not intend / was unlikely to be able to pay

english.notes:
(i) The 'relevant period' means the period between -
(a) the start of the period of two years ending with the application date; and (b) the determination date
(ii) A person is not guilty of an offence under this subsection if the acquisition or receipt of the property was in the ordinary course of a business carried on by the debtor at the time of the acquisition or receipt - section 251R(4)
(iii) In determining for the purposes of subsection (4) whether property is acquired or received in the ordinary course of a business carried on by the debtor, regard may be had, in particular, to the price paid for the property - section 251R(5)
(iv) In this section, references to disposing of property include pawning or pledging it; and references to acquiring or receiving property shall be read accordingly - section 251R(7)
(v) It is immaterial for the purposes of this section whether or not the debt relief order in question is revoked after the conduct constituting an offence takes place (but no offence is committed by virtue of conduct occurring after the order is revoked)
(vi) This offence was Inserted by section 108(1) of and Schedule 17 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (limit on magistrates' court powers to impose imprisonment), the reference to "twelve months" is to be read as a reference to "six months".

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
